script.title: A Better Way to Care — Welbuk

ananya.name: Dr. Ananya
ananya.description: Indian woman in her late 30s, clinic owner and doctor. Calm, confident and caring. Teal kurta beneath an open white coat (source). Shoulder-length black hair tied in a low bun with a few loose strands, slim build, small gold stud earrings, a stethoscope worn around her neck (never in use) in every scene where she wears the white coat (manga supplement, from the accepted reference sheet).

traits: Calm almond-shaped eyes with slightly heavy upper lids and a gentle downward outer corner
Soft, straight medium-thick eyebrows set fairly level
Oval face with a defined, slightly pointed chin and a small bindi-free forehead; small nose with a rounded tip
faceDesign.settingBasis: Source: Indian female clinic owner, late 30s, calm, confident, caring; teal kurta beneath white coat. Manga supplement: the three face traits, low bun hairstyle and gold studs, chosen to separate her from Meera.

meera.name: Meera
meera.description: Indian woman in her late 20s, clinic receptionist. Friendly and capable. Blue kurta (source). Long black hair in a single side braid over her left shoulder, round face, slim build, a thin silver bangle on the right wrist (manga supplement).

traits: Large, round bright eyes with clearly visible lower lash line
Thin, gently arched eyebrows set high above the eyes
Round face with full cheeks and a short soft chin; small dimple on the left cheek when smiling
faceDesign.settingBasis: Source: Indian female receptionist, late 20s, friendly and capable, blue kurta. Manga supplement: the three face traits, side braid and silver bangle.

ravi.name: Ravi
ravi.description: Indian man in his mid-30s, patient. Warm and approachable. Light green shirt (source). Short neat black hair with a side part, trimmed short beard, medium build, dark trousers, a simple wristwatch on the left wrist, small dark-brown shoulder bag (manga supplement).

traits: Warm, slightly narrow eyes that crease at the outer corners when he smiles
Thick, straight dark eyebrows close to the eyes
Square jaw framed by a short trimmed beard and a broad nose
faceDesign.settingBasis: Source: Indian male patient, mid-30s, warm, approachable, light green shirt. Manga supplement: the three face traits, beard, side part and wristwatch.

child.description: Symbolic family member in the vision scene. Child of about seven, short hair, orange T-shirt (manga supplement; the source only says 'child').

script.style: Full-colour, approachable Indian slice-of-life manga. Clean confident line art with varied line weight, soft flat cel shading, warm natural daylight, restrained blue and teal accents, simple readable backgrounds. Expressive but natural faces, precise hands. No photorealism, no glossy gradients, no surface microtexture. Absolutely no text, letters, logos, numbers, speech bubbles or captions inside the artwork; device screens show only abstract blank blocks and simple icons.
script.continuity: Keep Dr. Ananya, Meera and Ravi identical to their canonical reference sheets in face traits, hair, build, skin tone and clothing for the whole comic. Device screens never show readable text or real personal data. Pages 6 panels 2-3 are a future vision: soft pale-blue vignette border and lighter, airy palette so they never read as current features.

pages.scan: P1 (wide, top): caption at top left 'A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.' Outside a white clinic with a teal awning, a doctor (white coat, stethoscope, teal kurta, hair in a bun) stands at the glass door and waves an elderly woman in a lavender sari inside. Two patients sit on metal chairs at right with their backs to us. P2 (lower left): a receptionist (blue printed kurta, long braid) sits at a desk with a stack of ledgers, writes in an open book and holds a corded phone. She looks flustered (sweat drop, motion lines). Waiting patients in the foreground. Balloon 1 at top left: 'Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...'. Balloon 2 at right: 'I wish everything were easier to manage!' Both tails point to her. P3 (lower right): the doctor stands thoughtfully, hand on chin, with the receptionist small in the background on the phone. Balloon: 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.'
pages.observation: Reading order is clear. The two balloons in P2 are stacked left-high, right-low, so they read in the right order, and both tails go to the receptionist. P3's tail goes to the doctor. The caption names Dr. Ananya, and the door scene ties that name to the woman in the white coat. Her costume (coat, stethoscope, teal kurta, dark leggings, sandals, bun) matches between P1 and P3. The receptionist is never named here or anywhere later. That is fine for her role, but the reader only knows her as 'receptionist'. 'Our time belongs with patients' is understandable but slightly unidiomatic ('belongs to' or 'should go to patients' would be smoother). In P3 the doctor looks off rather than at the receptionist, so the line reads as musing to herself. That works. Small setting change: P1 and P2 show grey metal waiting chairs, while P3 shows blue padded chairs. A first-time reader probably won't notice. No skipped answer and no unreadable text.

pages.scan: P1 (wide, top): caption at top left 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' Brand box at top right 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic'. The doctor, seen from behind over her shoulder, types on a laptop showing an onboarding stepper and form. A sunset window, a coffee mug. P2 (middle left): the doctor at the laptop, hand on chin, smiling. Balloon: 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' P3 (middle right): the receptionist stands holding a phone with a calendar app, smiling. Balloon at top: 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' Brand box at bottom: 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff'. P4 (wide, bottom): the doctor seated at the laptop, fist raised a little, beside the receptionist standing with her phone. Balloon: 'One team. Better coordination.'
pages.observation: The time jump from day to sunset is shown only by the window light. The caption tells us what is happening, but not that it is later that day, or that the receptionist has joined the doctor in her office. This is readable but abrupt. The teal brand boxes look clearly different from the white narration captions, and that styling stays consistent through the book. Tails are correct (P2 doctor, P3 receptionist, P4 doctor). In P3 the 'And...' line follows naturally from P2, and the reader then sees the label box. Continuity: in P1 the doctor's stethoscope is not visible around her neck from this rear angle, but it is present in P2 and P4. In P4 her hair looks looser and shoulder-length rather than the tight bun of P1–P3. A small drift, probably acceptable. The change from the receptionist's paper ledger and landline on page 1 to a phone app here reads well as the before-and-after. No unreadable text.

pages.scan: P1 (top left): reception desk in daylight with a desktop computer. The receptionist, seen from behind on the left, looks up at a man (green shirt, brown messenger bag, beard) who comes through the glass door waving. His phone is on the counter. Balloon at top left, tail to him: 'Good morning! I'd like to see the doctor.' P2 (top right): the receptionist faces us and gestures, with the man's shoulder and the phone in his hand in the left foreground. Balloon: 'Of course. May I register your details for today's appointment?' P3 (middle, wide): the man leans on the counter, eyes closed, smiling and nodding. Balloon: 'Yes, please.' The receptionist types. P4 (bottom, wide): the man stands with his hand on his bag strap. The receptionist gestures toward the waiting chairs. Balloon: 'You're all set, Ravi. Please have a seat.'
pages.observation: The question-and-answer flow is clean: greeting, offer, 'Yes, please', done. No reply is skipped. Small logic gap 1: he asks to 'see the doctor', which sounds like a walk-in, but she answers 'today's appointment', which implies he has a booking. A first-time reader may hesitate briefly. Gap 2: she calls him 'Ravi', but he never gives his name, and the reader never sees details exchanged (no ID, no phone scan). The cut from 'Yes, please' to 'You're all set' skips the registration itself, so the name seems to come from nowhere. Showing a screen or the phone being used, or having him say his name, would close this gap. The new morning location is understandable from 'Good morning' and the daylight. The reception desk now has a desktop computer instead of the page 1 ledgers, which reads as the effect of onboarding. Phone continuity: on the counter in P1, in his hand in P2, on the counter in P3, not visible in P4. This is acceptable. The waiting chairs are teal, which differs from the grey chairs on page 1 (minor). Tails are correct. No unreadable text.

pages.scan: P1 (wide, top): consultation room. The doctor sits at the desk with her laptop closed and gestures to Ravi, who sits in a blue chair with wooden arms, his bag on the floor. Balloon by the doctor: 'Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.' P2 (middle left): Ravi rubs the back of his neck with a weary smile, the doctor's back in the left foreground. Balloon: 'I've been feeling tired lately.' P3 (middle right): narration caption at top: 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.' The doctor listens with clasped hands and a gentle smile, Ravi's back in the right foreground. Silent reaction. P4 (wide, bottom): the doctor gestures as she speaks. Balloon: 'We'll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.' Ravi nods (motion lines).
pages.observation: Reading order and tails are clear. The reverse shots in P2 and P3 keep the doctor on the left and Ravi on the right, so there is no axis confusion. P3 works as a silent listening beat, and the closed laptop supports the caption. Acting: the doctor smiles quite brightly in P3 and P4 in response to 'feeling tired', which comes across a little light, but it is not confusing. Continuity: his chair has wooden arms in P1, black plastic arms in P2, and blue-framed arms in P4. Ravi's watch, shirt and bag on the floor are consistent. The consultation ends without any outcome, so the reader never learns anything more about the tiredness complaint. This is acceptable for a short promotional piece, but it is an open thread (see page 05).

pages.scan: P1 (wide, top): back at the reception counter. The receptionist leans in and points at Ravi's phone. Balloon at top left, tail to her: 'Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.' P2 (middle left): close-up of Ravi holding the phone toward the reader, showing a calendar and heart app. Balloon: 'So I can keep useful information in one place?' Brand box at bottom left: 'WELBUK HEALTH for patients'. P3 (middle right): the receptionist behind the desk gestures toward Ravi's phone, with Ravi in the right foreground. Balloon: 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.' P4 (wide, bottom): caption 'A smoother visit. A more connected experience.' Outside the clinic, the doctor and receptionist wave from the glass doorway as Ravi walks away waving, bag on his shoulder.
pages.observation: The question in P2 is answered directly in P3. Nothing is skipped and the tails are correct. The move from the consultation room back to the reception desk has no transition, but the background (teal chairs, monitor, counter) makes it clear. As on page 04, the story never resolves the medical visit. We go straight from 'decide the next steps' to an app demo and a farewell, so a reader may feel the consultation thread was dropped. 'Let's walk through what is available to you' is immediately followed by the exit, without showing the walkthrough. This is acceptable as a time skip, but somewhat abrupt. The exterior in P4 matches page 1 (white wall, glimpse of the teal awning, glass doors), which neatly bookends the visit. Costumes are consistent. No unreadable text.

pages.scan: P1 (top left): Ravi on a train by the window, chin on hand, phone in his other hand, city skyline outside. Caption at top left: 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.' P2 (top right): brand box 'WELBUK VISION' at top left. A new older doctor (grey hair, glasses, stethoscope, jacket) in front of a large modern hospital, with dotted lines linking small clinic icons in the sky. Caption at bottom: 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.' P3 (middle, wide): brand box 'WELBUK VISION', then caption 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.' Ravi on a sofa with a woman in a yellow kurta holding a tablet with family icons and a heart, and a boy in an orange T-shirt. Ravi points at the screen with his arm around them. P4 (large, bottom): the receptionist (holding a phone), the doctor and Ravi (waving, bag) stand together in front of the clinic. Brand box at top right: 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health'. Caption at bottom left: 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.'
pages.observation: This page changes from story to brand vision. The order is still readable (label, then caption, in each panel). Issues for a first-time reader: (1) P1 has no 'WELBUK VISION' label, unlike P2 and P3, so it is unclear whether Ravi is really travelling now or this is imagined. 'Tomorrow... may' points to speculation, and 'us' has no clear referent (Ravi? patients in general?). (2) The older specialist in P2 is a brand-new character with no introduction or link to the story. (3) The woman and boy in P3 are new and unnamed, and family is implied only by the hug and the word 'family'. The woman's face and hair are close enough to the doctor's and receptionist's look that a reader could briefly wonder whether she is one of them. Her different clothes help. (4) Ravi wears the same green shirt in the train and sofa scenes, which blurs the line between present and vision. (5) In P4 the patient poses as part of the clinic group, which reads as a closing ad image rather than a story moment. That is fine for a promotional comic, but it is a tonal jump. No unreadable text. The brand-box styling matches pages 02 and 05.
